# rsmack

> The Rust proc-macro factory: write the exec function, get a documented macro.
> edoc, wrap, seanum, folder_iso_struct, and megamac in one dependency.

Routes are relative to the site root. Rendered pages are plain HTML.

# rsmack — the Rust proc-macro factory | rsmack

URL: //

rsmack — the Rust proc-macro factory
Write the exec function, get a documented macro.
Start the tutorial
rsmack is a Rust proc-macro factory. You write a pub struct Args with doc comments and a pub fn exec that does the transformation; the framework handles entrypoint generation, payload-protocol selection, documentation extraction, error plumbing, and file codegen. One cargo add rsmack installs every shipped macro.
The workspace ships five macros and the toolkit behind them:
edoc — documentation from constants, with typed const-expression evaluation
wrap — field type wrappers that accept any type
seanum — SeaORM active enums with discriminants and migrations
folder_iso_struct — inline compile-time folder mirroring
megamac — the signature-driven factory that generates all of the above and your own macros
Everything rests on rsmack-utils, which provides the ExecEnv/Logr diagnostics pair — a syn::Error-based, panic-free replacement for the abandoned proc-macro-error2 crate.
Choose your path
Section titled “Choose your path”
Use the shipped macros
Add rsmack, annotate a struct, and read your docs in cargo doc. Start with the getting-started tutorial.
Write your own macro
Declare megamac!(kind = Func, name = my_macro), write src/impls/my_macro.rs, done. Follow the custom macro guide.
Look up an option
Every attribute option, default, and error message is tabulated in the Reference section.
Understand the design
Read how the signature-driven payload protocol and the diagnostics philosophy shape the workspace.
Start the tutorial
Requirements
Section titled “Requirements”
Rust 1.94 or newer (edition 2024, pinned by sea-orm 2)
A crate where you want to use or author macros
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
Getting startedInstall rsmack and generate your first documented macro in ten minutes.

# Architecture | rsmack

URL: /explanation/architecture/

Architecture
The rsmack workspace is a stack of nine Cargo crates: five user-facing macros, one facade, the factory that generates them, the toolkit everything shares, and two development-only crates. Understanding the layering explains why a macro author needs both rsmack-megamac and rsmack-utils.
Directorypackages
rsmack — facade: every macro behind one feature-gated dependency
rsmack-edoc — docs from constants (generated by megamac)
rsmack-wrap — field type wrappers (generated by megamac)
rsmack-seanum — SeaORM active enums (generated by megamac)
rsmack-fs — folder mirroring (generated by megamac)
rsmack-megamac — the macro factory itself
rsmack-utils — ExecEnv, Logr, entrypoint drivers, fs helpers
rsmack-example-macros — living example crate (not published)
rsmack-ui-tests — trybuild diagnostic snapshots (not published)
The facade
Section titled “The facade”
The rsmack crate is a re-export shim. Each macro sits behind a feature, and full (the default) enables all of them:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">[</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">features</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">default = [</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"full"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">full = [</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"edoc"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"wrap"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"seanum"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"fs"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"megamac"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">]</span></div></div></code>
Depending on rsmack gives you every macro through one import surface; depending on the standalone crates (rsmack-edoc, rsmack-wrap, …) keeps compile times down when you need one macro.
Every shipped macro is megamac-generated
Section titled “Every shipped macro is megamac-generated”
The shipped macros do not hand-write their entrypoints. Each crate’s src/lib.rs contains a declaration like:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">megamac!</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(kind </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Attr</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, name </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> edoc, doc </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"readme"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">);</span></div></div></code>
The entrypoint function, the payload parsing, and the generated documentation all come from the same machinery you use to write your own macros. When the factory improves — richer docs, faster memoization — every shipped macro inherits the improvement.
Why a macro author needs two dependencies
Section titled “Why a macro author needs two dependencies”
Proc-macro crates cannot be imported as plain modules, so the code megamac! generates must name its dependencies by path. The generated entrypoints call rsmack_utils::exec::* drivers and exec receives rsmack_utils::megamac::ExecEnv — which is why authoring with megamac requires a direct rsmack-utils dependency alongside rsmack-megamac.
Quality infrastructure
Section titled “Quality infrastructure”
The workspace enforces its posture mechanically: clippy::pedantic denied with zero allows, 100% line coverage via cargo-llvm-cov, every error path snapshotted with trybuild, parsers fuzzed with cargo fuzz, criterion benchmarks per macro, git-cliff changelogs, and tag-driven releases to crates.io. The diagnostics philosophy explains the no-panic guarantee behind it.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
The payload protocolHow an exec signature selects the entrypoint shape.

# Diagnostics philosophy | rsmack

URL: /explanation/diagnostics-philosophy/

Diagnostics philosophy
A panicking proc macro turns user code into an internal compiler error — the worst failure mode a library can produce. rsmack’s design goal is that arbitrary input becomes a compile_error!, never an ICE.
The problem with proc-macro-error2
Section titled “The problem with proc-macro-error2”
For years the Rust ecosystem accepted panics as a proc-macro control-flow mechanism: proc-macro-error and its maintained fork proc-macro-error2 catch panics and convert them into compiler errors. rsmack dropped the dependency in 0.20 and replaced it with a syn::Error-based collector: Logr. There is no unwinding and no panic catching anywhere in the workspace, and the generated code carries no #[proc_macro_error] attribute.
Two severities, one pass
Section titled “Two severities, one pass”
Severity Mechanism Use when
Fatal
Return a syn::Error with ?; render through ExecEnv::finish_result
Expansion is meaningless — unreadable file, unparsable item
Collected
Logr::emit_error, flushed by finish as compile_error! tokens
Output is still usable — one bad field should not hide the others
Collected diagnostics let one expansion report every problem in a single pass. edoc leans on this: a tuple with two broken elements produces two prefixed errors, and the healthy elements still render their docs.
The style guide
Section titled “The style guide”
Messages follow docs/ERROR_STYLE.md in the repository: start with the failure, use consistent verbs (Failed to ..., Only ... supported, Unsupported ..., Invalid ...), backtick identifiers, and drop the trailing period. The error messages reference catalogues the results.
Proving the guarantee
Section titled “Proving the guarantee”
Three mechanisms keep the no-panic promise honest:
Fuzzing — four cargo fuzz targets feed arbitrary bytes to the parsers (edoc constants source, edoc meta, wrap meta, megamac meta). Invalid input must produce a clean error, valid input must resolve or report issues — never panic.
Snapshot tests — every error path is pinned with trybuild in packages/rsmack-ui-tests, so both the wording and the promise fail a review if they regress.
Zero-allow pedantic lints — clippy::pedantic is denied workspace-wide with no allows, closing the common paths to accidental unwrap/expect.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
Error messages referenceEvery snapshotted diagnostic with its trigger.

# The payload protocol | rsmack

URL: /explanation/payload-protocol/

The payload protocol
Most macro frameworks ask you to declare the payload shape twice: once in a configuration struct and once in the code that parses it. megamac derives everything from the exec signature — the signature is the configuration.
How inference works
Section titled “How inference works”
At expansion time, megamac! locates exec in src/impls/<name>.rs, strips the trailing &ExecEnv parameter, and counts what remains. The last path segment of each parameter’s type drives the decision, so proc_macro2::TokenStream and a re-exported TokenStream are recognized equally.
Remaining parameters Protocol Entry point generated
args: Args
darling meta parsing, docs extracted from Args
func_entrypoint
input: TokenStream
raw payload for DSL macros
func_raw_entrypoint
args: Args, item: syn::Item
darling meta plus parsed item
attr_entrypoint
input: TokenStream, item: syn::Item
raw payload plus parsed item
attr_raw_entrypoint
item: syn::DeriveInput
derive — no payload, no # Parameters docs
derive_entrypoint
The parsed item type for attribute macros stays signature-inferred: annotate the item with whatever type you accept, and the generated entrypoint parses it for you.
Why darling by default
Section titled “Why darling by default”
Darling-parsed payloads give macro users named arguments (greeting!(who = "world")) and give macro authors self-documenting configuration: the Args struct’s doc comments become the generated macro’s # Parameters section, and Option<T> or #[darling(default)] fields are automatically marked (optional). The documentation cannot drift from the behavior because both come from the same source.
Why raw payloads exist
Section titled “Why raw payloads exist”
DSL macros — shout!(hello megamac) — take token soup, not named arguments. Changing the signature to exec(input: TokenStream, env: &ExecEnv) selects the raw driver; there is nothing else to configure. The one fatal overlap: declaring args = "MyArgs" while the signature takes a raw TokenStream is rejected, because the two settings contradict each other.
Derives have no payload
Section titled “Derives have no payload”
kind = Derive generates a derive macro named after the PascalCase of name — type_name produces #[derive(TypeName)]. Derives receive the DeriveInput and document no parameters.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
megamac referenceThe invocation grammar and doc-generation rules.

# Performance | rsmack

URL: /explanation/performance/

Performance
Proc macros sit on the compile critical path: every keystroke in an editor re-expands them. The rsmack design treats expansion cost as a first-class constraint.
Typed const evaluation
Section titled “Typed const evaluation”
edoc evaluates constant expressions with machine-typed values — i128, f64, bool, byte strings — and converts to a string once, at doc assembly. There are no per-operation string round-trips, which is why a typed evaluation such as concat!("v", 1 + 2, "-", 3 * 4) costs 4.6 µs end to end.
Process-global caches
Section titled “Process-global caches”
Two memoization layers share the same staleness discipline — a (path, mtime, len) key that re-parses a file only after it actually changed:
Constants files (edoc): N annotated items against one src/consts.rs cost one parse; warm expansions against the cached file run at 63 µs for a full 8-field struct.
Impl files (megamac): the impls/<name>.rs analysis (payload protocol, args fields, intro docs) is cached per (path, mtime, len, kind, args_override). Warm macro generation measures 15–18 µs, down from about 1.35 ms — a roughly 90× improvement that pays off most in rust-analyzer re-expansions and test loops.
Feature-gated syn
Section titled “Feature-gated syn”
rsmack-utils compiles against syn without the full feature. Only the crates that genuinely parse full items — structs, enums, whole files — opt in, so the toolkit’s compile-time weight stays at the default feature set.
Diagnostics overhead
Section titled “Diagnostics overhead”
The collector adds about 160 ns on the happy path (finish_result around a valid expansion) and roughly 4 µs to collect and flush four errors. Error handling is effectively free, which is what makes the collect-everything UX affordable.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
Benchmarks referenceEvery criterion measurement with notes.

# Roadmap | rsmack

URL: /explanation/roadmap/

Roadmap
The 1.0.0 release closed the v2 redesign recorded in docs/DESIGN_v2.md: “any Rust developer authors a production-grade, fully documented, panic-free proc macro in under twenty lines, and installs every shipped macro with one cargo add rsmack.” This page summarizes what shipped and what the repository tracks as remaining work in docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md.
Shipped in 1.0.0
Section titled “Shipped in 1.0.0”
Signature-driven payload protocol with the doc = "none" option and richer generated docs
The rsmack facade crate
megamac impl-file caching with the roughly 90× warm-expansion win
edoc typed const evaluation, path-aware constants, enum-variant and item-level docs
wrap accepting every type (the v1 unsupported-type error path was deleted)
seanum minimal default derives, explicit discriminants with duplicate detection, rename_all, enum_name
folder_iso_struct inline emission — no build-script flavor in the macro itself
ExecEnv::new replacing the bon builder, shared staleness_key
No backward compatibility The v2 redesign deliberately broke the 0.x API surface: signature changes, derive payload removal, and the ExecEnv::new constructor are all recorded in the 1.0.0 changelog.
Remaining backlog
Section titled “Remaining backlog”
Area Item Impact Effort
Performance
Cache megamac impl-file source reads
Low
Low
Performance
Precompute pascal_options per process
Low
Low
Modularity
Split rsmack-utils by concern
Medium
Medium
Fuzzing
Scheduled fuzzing in CI
Medium
Medium
edoc
Richer const evaluation — structs, include!
Low
High
seanum
Const-expression discriminants
Low
Medium
megamac
Playground expansion of macro invocations (needs cargo-expand)
Medium
High
folder_iso_struct
Per-nested-struct derives
Low
Low
The utils split is deferred because generated code embeds rsmack_utils:: paths — a physical split would break every published crate at once.

# Document from constants (edoc) | rsmack

URL: /guides/docs-from-constants/

Document from constants (edoc)
Use edoc when documentation must stay in sync with code: version strings from constants, build numbers from env!, or combined tags from concat!. edoc evaluates #[edoc((...))] tuples into real #[doc] attributes on struct fields, enum variants, and the item itself.
Point edoc at your constants file
Section titled “Point edoc at your constants file”
The from argument names the module path that maps to a file under your crate’s src/ directory — :: becomes / and .rs is appended:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc(from </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> consts)] </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// reads src/consts.rs</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc(from </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> impls</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">doc_consts)] </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// reads src/impls/doc_consts.rs</span></div></div></code>
self is not handled as a path segment — write the path relative to src/ without it.
Evaluate tuples of elements
Section titled “Evaluate tuples of elements”
Annotate fields or variants with a tuple of elements. Each element is a string literal, a constant reference, or a const expression:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">use</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">rsmack_edoc</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">edoc;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc(from </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> consts)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Client</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc((</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Client "</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">APP</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">" tag "</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">TAG</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">" build "</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, 2 </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">*</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> 21))]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">name</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">String</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
Supported element kinds include:
Literals: &str, integers, f64, bool, char, and byte strings
Arithmetic, bitwise, shift, logic, and comparison operators
Casts with rustc semantics (300 as u8 wraps to 44, float-to-int saturates)
The macros concat!, env!, and option_env!
Reference constants by full path or bare name
Section titled “Reference constants by full path or bare name”
A reference resolves against the full module path first. A bare name falls back to a workspace-wide search — unique names resolve, ambiguous names report every candidate:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc((</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Qualified: "</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, impls</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">doc_consts</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">APP</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">))]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc((</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Bare: "</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">APP</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">))] </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// resolves when APP is unique in the file</span></div></div></code>
Ambiguity produces Ambiguous const 'NAME', qualify the path: 'a::NAME', 'b::NAME' — see the error message reference.
Document enum variants and the item itself
Section titled “Document enum variants and the item itself”
Variant tuples work like field tuples. For the item itself, add a separate #[edoc((...))] attribute next to from:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc(from </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> consts)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc((</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"The "</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">APP</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">" client"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">))]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">enum</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">State</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc((</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Idle since "</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">TAG</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">))]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Idle</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Busy</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
Keep one constants file per crate
Section titled “Keep one constants file per crate”
Resolution is memoized per file with a process-global cache keyed by (path, mtime, len). Annotating N items against one src/consts.rs costs one parse; every use of the cached file re-emits any non-fatal issues it contains, so nothing hides.
Verify the result
Section titled “Verify the result”
Terminal window
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">cargo</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">doc</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--no-deps</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--open</span></div></div></code>
Every evaluated tuple appears as rendered text on the field, variant, or item page.
Next steps

# Handle macro errors | rsmack

URL: /guides/handle-errors/

Handle macro errors
Macros that panic produce ICEs — internal compiler errors — in user builds. The rsmack-utils diagnostics pair replaces panics with structured reporting: fatal problems return a syn::Error, recoverable problems are collected and flushed together, and every message carries your macro’s prefix.
Return fatal errors with finish_result
Section titled “Return fatal errors with finish_result”
When expansion cannot continue, return a syn::Error with ? and hand the Result to ExecEnv::finish_result:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">fn</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">exec</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(args</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Args</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, env</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">&</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">ExecEnv</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">) </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">-></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">TokenStream</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">env</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">.</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">finish_result</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">run</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(args))</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">fn</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">run</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(args</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Args</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">) </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">-></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">syn</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Result</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"><</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">TokenStream</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">let</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> path </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> args</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">.</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">path;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">let</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> file </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">std</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">fs</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">read_to_string</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">&</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">path)</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">.</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">map_err</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">|</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">e</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">|</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">syn</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Error</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">new</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(path</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">.</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">span</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(), </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">format!</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Failed to read file `{path}`: {e}"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)))</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">?</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// ...</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Ok</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">quote</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">quote!</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {})</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
The error is rendered as a compile_error! at the offending span, prefixed #[your_crate::your_macro].
Collect non-fatal errors with Logr
Section titled “Collect non-fatal errors with Logr”
When one bad field should not hide the others, collect errors with Logr::emit_error and flush at the end. ExecEnv already owns a Logr; env.finish(...) flushes the collected errors as compile_error! tokens appended to otherwise valid output:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">for</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> field </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">in</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> args</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">.</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">fields {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">if</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> field</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">.</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">ident</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">.</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">is_none</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">() {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">env</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">.</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">logr</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">.</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">emit_error</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(field</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">.</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">span</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(), </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Only named fields supported"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">);</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">env</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">.</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">finish</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">generate_output</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">())</span></div></div></code>
One broken item reports every problem in a single pass — the UX that proc-macro-error2 pioneered, without the abandoned dependency.
Write messages in the house style
Section titled “Write messages in the house style”
The workspace style guide, enforced by snapshot tests, keeps every diagnostic predictable:
Rule Example
Start with the failure
Failed to read constants file
Failed to <verb> ... for read/parse failures
Failed to parse macro_impl_src
Only <thing> supported for constraints
Only named struct supported
Unsupported `<thing>` `<value>` for unknown variants
Unsupported MacroKind `Nope`
Backtick identifiers and paths
Unresolved const ident `NOPE`
No trailing period
…follows rustc convention
Every message the shipped macros can emit is catalogued in the error messages reference.
Never panic
Section titled “Never panic”
expect, unwrap, and panic! are forbidden in macro code paths. Arbitrary user input must become a compile_error!, not an ICE — the workspace fuzzes its parsers (fuzz/) to keep that promise.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
rsmack-utils referenceThe ExecEnv and Logr method tables and the five entrypoint drivers.
Edit page
Previous
Write your own macroNext
Preview with the playground

# Mirror a folder | rsmack

URL: /guides/mirror-a-folder/

Mirror a folder
Use folder_iso_struct when a struct must mirror a folder of modules: game levels, screen definitions, plugin registries. The folder is scanned at macro-expansion time and the mirrored struct is emitted inline — one attribute, zero build scripts, nothing in OUT_DIR.
Declare the struct and the folder
Section titled “Declare the struct and the folder”
Start from a folder of modules that your crate already declares:
Directorysrc
Directorylevels
mod.rs
button.rs
beta_gamma.rs
main.rs
src/main.rs
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">mod</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">levels</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">use</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">rsmack_fs</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">folder_iso_struct;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[folder_iso_struct(folder </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"levels"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, vis </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"pub"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, derives(</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Debug"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">))]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Levels</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// The declared fields are a sketch only: the mirror is generated from the folder.</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[expect(dead_code)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">alpha</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> (),</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
The macro scans src/levels/, skips mod.rs, and generates one field per file stem. button.rs becomes a field button of type crate::levels::button::Button; beta_gamma.rs becomes beta_gamma: crate::levels::beta_gamma::BetaGamma. The field names are snake_case and the type names are PascalCase conversions of the stem.
Go recursive for subdirectories
Section titled “Go recursive for subdirectories”
With recursive = true, each subdirectory becomes an inline pub mod <name> holding its own mirrored struct, named after the PascalCase of the directory:
Directorysrc
Directoryui
mod.rs
Directoryscreens
login.rs
settings.rs
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[folder_iso_struct(folder </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"ui/screens"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, recursive </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> true, derives(</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Debug"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">))]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Screens</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {}</span></div></div></code>
What carries over
Section titled “What carries over”
The annotated struct’s attributes and visibility are copied onto every generated struct.
derives("Debug", ...) injects extra derives on every generated struct.
The declared fields are discarded — the folder is the source of truth.
Tuple structs report Only named struct supported.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
folder_iso_struct referenceEvery option, the scanning rules, and the fatal errors.
Write your own macroBuild a macro like this in a dozen lines with megamac.

Previous
SeaORM enums (seanum)Next
Write your own macro

# Preview with the playground | rsmack

URL: /guides/preview-with-playground/

Preview with the playground
The playground binary in rsmack-megamac prints the code a megamac! call would generate — the entrypoint function and its documentation — before you compile anything. It reads your src/impls/<name>.rs and replays the same analysis the macro performs, memoization included.
Run it from the rsmack workspace
Section titled “Run it from the rsmack workspace”
Inside the rsmack repository:
Terminal window
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">cargo</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">run</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">-p</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">rsmack-megamac</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--bin</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">playground</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--kind</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">Attr</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--name</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">edoc</span></div></div></code>
Run it in your own crate
Section titled “Run it in your own crate”
The binary ships with the published rsmack-megamac crate. Install it once:
Terminal window
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">cargo</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">install</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">rsmack-megamac</span></div></div></code>
Then run it from your crate root, where --src-dir defaults to $CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/src:
Terminal window
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">playground</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--kind</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">Func</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--name</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">greeting</span></div></div></code>
The output is the generated entrypoint source — the proc-macro function signature and the doc comment assembled from your Args docs — printed to stdout.
Flags
Section titled “Flags”
Flag Default Meaning
--kind
required
Func, Attr, or Derive
--name
required
The macro name declared in megamac!
--src-dir
$CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/src
Where impls/<name>.rs is looked up
--impls
impls
The implementation module name
--args
Args
The args struct name
--doc
inline
readme, inline, or none
Errors exit non-zero with error: <message>; a missing or unexpected argument prints the usage line.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
megamac referenceHow the payload protocol is inferred from your exec signature.

Previous
Handle macro errorsNext

# SeaORM enums (seanum) | rsmack

URL: /guides/seaorm-enums/

SeaORM enums (seanum)
Use seanum when an enum must live in a database through SeaORM. The macro generates the DeriveActiveEnum plumbing with deliberately minimal default derives and adds integer discriminants or a migration helper on demand.
Define a string-backed enum
Section titled “Define a string-backed enum”
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">use</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">rsmack_seanum</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">seanum;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[seanum(</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">rs_type </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"String"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">db_type </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"String(sea_orm::sea_query::StringLen::None)"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">rename_all </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"snake_case"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">derives(</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"::serde::Serialize"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"::serde::Deserialize"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[derive(</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Default</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">enum</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">SwitchAction</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[default]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[seanum(rename </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"send_email"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">SendEmail</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">SendSms</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
The generated values are send_email (explicit rename wins over rename_all) and send_sms. The default derives are Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, EnumIter, and DeriveActiveEnum — serde and fake support is opt-in through derives(...), never a hidden dependency.
Use integer discriminants
Section titled “Use integer discriminants”
With an integer rs_type from i8 through u64 (plus isize/usize), the macro adds #[repr(...)], a #[sea_orm(num_value = N)] on every variant, and a value-based TryFrom:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[seanum(rs_type </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"i32"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, db_type </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Integer"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">enum</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Level</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Low</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">10</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Medium</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// continues from 11</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">High</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
Explicit discriminants are honored and later variants continue from them. Duplicates are reported as a collected error and the TryFrom is skipped, while the enum itself still compiles.
Generate the migration helper
Section titled “Generate the migration helper”
migration = true emits a migration_column_def() helper for use with sea-orm-migration:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[seanum(rs_type </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"String"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, db_type </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Text"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, migration </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> true)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">enum</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Status</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Active</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Retired</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
The helper maps the db_type to the matching ColumnDef method — Text, Integer, BigInt, Boolean, DateTime, and twelve more are covered.
Rename values consistently
Section titled “Rename values consistently”
rename_all accepts exactly seven cases: snake_case, camelCase, PascalCase, kebab-case, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, lowercase, and UPPERCASE. An unknown case is a fatal error at expansion time. enum_name = "..." overrides the table name, which defaults to the snake-cased enum name.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
seanum referenceEvery option, the integer-rs_type behavior, and the db_type mapping table.
Mirror a folderMirror a folder of modules into a struct at compile time.

# Wrap field types | rsmack

URL: /guides/wrap-field-types/

Wrap field types
Use wrap to produce draft, builder, or storage variants of a struct without hand-writing parallel types. One attribute wraps every field of a named struct in the generic type you choose.
Wrap a whole struct
Section titled “Wrap a whole struct”
Set the default wrapper with with — a bare identifier or a string literal both work:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">use</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">rsmack_wrap</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">wrap;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[wrap(with </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Option</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">User</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">name</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">String</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// becomes Option<String></span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">tags</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Vec</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"><</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">String</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">>, </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// becomes Option<Vec<String>></span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
Control individual fields
Section titled “Control individual fields”
Per-field #[wrap(...)] attributes override the default. The skip option leaves a field untouched, a per-field with swaps the wrapper, and map replaces the inner type altogether:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[wrap(with </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Option</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">User</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">name</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">String</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[wrap(skip)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">untouched</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">&</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">'</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">static</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">str</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// stays &'static str</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[wrap(with </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Box"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">boxed</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">String</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// becomes Box<String></span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[wrap(with </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Vec"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, map </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"u8"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">raw</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">String</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// becomes Vec<u8></span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
Any type wraps
Section titled “Any type wraps”
The transformation rewrites the field type to Wrapper<Inner>, so every type expression wraps: paths, slices, tuples, arrays, references, raw pointers, function pointers, and trait objects:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[wrap(with </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Option</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Inputs</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">borrowed</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">&</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">'</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">static</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">str</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// Option<&'static str></span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">pointer</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">*const</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">u8</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// Option<*const u8></span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">callback</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">fn</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">u8</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">) </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">-></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">bool</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// Option<fn(u8) -> bool></span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">object</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Box</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"><</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">dyn</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Send</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">>, </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// Option<Box<dyn Send>></span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
Keep serde derives after wrap
Section titled “Keep serde derives after wrap”
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[wrap(with </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Option</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[derive(serde</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Serialize</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, serde</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Deserialize</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">User</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">name</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">String</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
Mind the constraints
Section titled “Mind the constraints”
Only named-field structs are supported; tuple and unit structs report Only named struct supported.
Generics and where-clauses pass through untouched — only the fields section of the struct is rewritten.
Non-wrap attributes are preserved; the #[wrap(...)] attributes themselves are consumed.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
wrap referenceEvery option, default, and error message in one table.
SeaORM enums (seanum)Generate active enums with discriminants and migrations.

Docs from constants (edoc)Next

# Write your own macro | rsmack

URL: /guides/write-your-own-macro/

Write your own macro
Use megamac to author your own proc macro. You declare the macro with one megamac! call and write an exec function in src/impls/<name>.rs; the framework generates the #[proc_macro] entrypoint, parses the payload, extracts the documentation, and wires the diagnostics.
1. Create a proc-macro crate
Section titled “1. Create a proc-macro crate”
Terminal window
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">cargo</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">new</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">my-macros</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--lib</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">cd</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">my-macros</span></div></div></code>
Mark the crate as a proc-macro crate and add both rsmack dependencies — rsmack-megamac for the codegen and rsmack-utils because the generated code routes through its entrypoint drivers:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">[</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">lib</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">proc-macro = </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">true</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">[</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">dependencies</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">rsmack-megamac = </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"1"</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">rsmack-utils = </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"1"</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">darling = </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"0.24"</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">proc-macro2 = </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"1"</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">quote = </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"1"</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">syn = </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"3"</span></div></div></code>
2. Declare the macro
Section titled “2. Declare the macro”
src/lib.rs
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">use</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">rsmack_megamac</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">megamac;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">

</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// Generates a function-like `greeting!` macro documented from</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// src/impls/greeting.rs's `Args` doc comments.</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">megamac!</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(kind </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Func</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, name </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> greeting);</span></div></div></code>
3. Write the implementation
Section titled “3. Write the implementation”
The convention is src/impls/<name>.rs with a documented Args struct and an exec function:
src/impls/greeting.rs
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">use</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">darling</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">FromMeta</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">use</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">proc_macro2</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">TokenStream</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">use</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">rsmack_utils</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">megamac</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">ExecEnv</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">/// Greeting configuration</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[derive(</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Debug</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">FromMeta</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Args</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">/// Recipient of the greeting</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> who</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">String</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">fn</span><span {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">let</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> who </span><span {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">const</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">GREETING</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">&</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">str</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">);</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">})</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
Doc comments become the generated macro’s documentation: the struct doc is the intro, and each field doc becomes a # Parameters bullet with its type. Fields that are Option<T> or carry #[darling(default)] are marked (optional).
4. Use it
Section titled “4. Use it”
From a crate that depends on my-macros:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">my_macros</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">greeting!</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(who </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"world"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">);</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">assert_eq!</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(</span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">GREETING</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Hello world!"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">);</span></div></div></code>
Pick the macro kind
Section titled “Pick the macro kind”
Declaration Generates exec receives
megamac!(kind = Func, name = x)
x! function-like macro
darling-parsed Args or raw tokens
megamac!(kind = Attr, name = x)
#[x] attribute macro
the item plus darling Args or raw tokens
megamac!(kind = Derive, name = x)
derive named X (PascalCase of name)
the DeriveInput only
Switch to a raw-payload DSL macro
Section titled “Switch to a raw-payload DSL macro”
Change the exec signature to take a raw TokenStream — the signature is the configuration:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// src/impls/shout.rs — declared with megamac!(kind = Func, name = shout);</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">use</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">proc_macro2</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">TokenStream</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">use</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">rsmack_utils</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">megamac</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">ExecEnv</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">fn</span><span {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">let</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> shouted </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">str</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> #shouted; })</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">my_macros</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">shout!</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(hello megamac);</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">assert_eq!</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(</span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">SHOUTED</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"HELLO MEGAMAC"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">);</span></div></div></code>
Choose the documentation source
Section titled “Choose the documentation source”
The doc knob controls the generated documentation: doc = "readme" embeds the calling crate’s README.md through include_str!, doc = "inline" generates only the parameter docs (the default, with no README dependency), and doc = "none" emits no docs. Optional impls = "my_impls" and args = "MyArgs" rename the implementation module and args struct.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
megamac referenceThe full invocation grammar, signature protocols, and cache behavior.
Handle macro errorsReport fatal and collected diagnostics without panicking.

# Benchmarks reference | rsmack

URL: /reference/benchmarks/

Benchmarks reference
Expansion benchmarks run with criterion 0.8.2 (mean of 100 samples, Rust 1.99, ubuntu-latest-class runners). Reproduce with:
Terminal window
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">cargo</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">bench</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--workspace</span></div></div></code>
Results
Section titled “Results”
Benchmark Mean Notes

ExecEnv::new

megamac/exec_attr_generation
18 µs
warm, cached impl analysis
What the numbers buy you
Section titled “What the numbers buy you”
The memoization win: the 0.20 reference run measured megamac/exec_*_generation at about 1.35 ms per expansion. The impl-file memo brings warm expansions to 15–18 µs — roughly a 90× improvement, most visible in rust-analyzer re-checks and test loops.
Shared constants files: memoized consts save N × 28 µs for N structs annotating against one src/consts.rs.
Diagnostics are effectively free: about 160 ns of driver overhead plus roughly 4 µs to collect and flush four errors.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
PerformanceWhy the caches and the typed evaluator are fast.
