# edoc reference | rsmack

URL: /reference/edoc/

edoc reference
edoc is an attribute macro — generated by megamac!(kind = Attr, name = edoc, doc = "readme") — that evaluates #[edoc((...))] tuples of string literals, constant references, and const expressions into real #[doc] attributes. Crate path: rsmack_edoc (facade: rsmack::edoc, feature edoc).
Signature
Section titled “Signature”
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc(from </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> path</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">to</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">consts)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc((</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Element "</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">CONST</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">" expression "</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, 2 </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">*</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> 21))]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Item</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> { </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">...</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> }</span></div></div></code>
Item arguments
Section titled “Item arguments”
from optional
Section titled “from optional ”
Type: syn::Path
Default: none — without from, only item-level tuples are evaluated
Meaning: module path that locates the constants file; :: maps to / and .rs is appended relative to the calling crate’s src/ — impls::sub::consts reads src/impls/sub/consts.rs
Constraint: self is not handled as a path segment
Example: from = consts
item-level tuple optional
Section titled “item-level tuple optional ”
Type: a syn::Expr that must parse as a tuple
Meaning: elements concatenated into the item’s #[doc]; pre-existing docs on the item are overwritten
Placement: a separate #[edoc((...))] attribute next to #[edoc(from = ...)]
Applicable items
Section titled “Applicable items”
Only structs and enums carry field docs. Any other item is fatal: Only structs and enums supported, other items cannot carry field docs.
Const-expression grammar
Section titled “Const-expression grammar”
Elements are evaluated with a typed evaluator mirroring rustc’s min_const_eval subset. Values keep machine types (i128, f64, bool, char, Vec<u8>, String) until doc assembly — there are no per-operation string round-trips.
Kind Supported forms
Literals
&str, integers (i128 range), floats (f64), bool, char, byte strings
Unary
-x, !x (dereference * is unsupported)
Arithmetic
+ - * / % (checked; div-by-zero and overflow reported)
Bitwise
& | ^
Shifts
<< >> (amount validated as u32)
Logic
&& ||
Comparison
== != < <= > >= (same-kind operands; bool only ==/!=)
Casts
as i8..i128, u8..u128, isize, usize, f32, f64 — int narrowing wraps two’s-complement (300 as u8 → 44), float-to-int saturates, NaN → 0
Macros
concat! (renders non-strings too), env! (unset variable is an error), option_env! (defaults to empty string)
Anything else reports Unsupported const expression '...' or Unsupported const macro 'X!' as a collected error.
Constants-file resolution
Section titled “Constants-file resolution”
The file is parsed as a real syn::File; a visitor walks const items through the module stack and keys each by full path (nested::DEEP).
Const-to-const references resolve lazily with per-key memoization; cycles report Cyclic const dependency involving 'X'.
A reference matches the exact full path first. A bare name falls back to a unique match; several candidates report Ambiguous const 'NAME', qualify the path: 'a::NAME', 'b::NAME', no candidate reports Unresolved const ident 'X'.
Caching
Section titled “Caching”
Process-global cache keyed by file path, validated against (mtime, len).
N annotated items against one constants file cost one parse.
Non-fatal issues stored with the cached file re-emit on every use.
Error behavior
Section titled “Error behavior”
Fatal (returned through ExecEnv::finish_result): unreadable constants file, unparsable constants file, unsupported item kinds.
Collected (flushed together at the end): broken tuple payloads, unsupported expressions, unresolved/ambiguous constants. Every broken expression of an item reports in one pass; the failing element renders a Missing: placeholder in the doc while the rest still materialize.
Example
Section titled “Example”
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">use</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">rsmack_edoc</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">edoc;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc(from </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> consts)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc((</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"The "</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">APP</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">" client"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">))]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">enum</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">State</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc((</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Idle since "</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">TAG</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">))]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Idle</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Busy</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
Document from constantsA task-focused guide with a working setup.

# Error messages reference | rsmack

URL: /reference/error-messages/

Error messages reference
Every diagnostic from an rsmack macro is a compile_error! — never a panic. The message style is enforced by trybuild snapshots in packages/rsmack-ui-tests, so an accidental wording change fails review.
Message format
Section titled “Message format”
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292e;--1:#e1e4e8">error: #[<crate>::<macro>] <message></span></div></div></code>
Real prefixes: #[rsmack_edoc::edoc], #[rsmack_wrap::wrap], #[rsmack_seanum::seanum], #[rsmack_fs::folder_iso_struct], #[rsmack_megamac::megamac]. Spans point at the offending tokens, or at the whole invocation for call-site fatals.
Message style rules
Section titled “Message style rules”
Start with the failure — no Error: decoration, no emoji.
Consistent verbs: Failed to `<verb>` ... for read/parse failures, Only `<thing>` supported for constraints, Unsupported `<thing>` `<value>` for unknown variants, Invalid `<thing>` ... for value-construction problems.
Backtick identifiers, paths, and values; never quote whole sentences.
No trailing period, following rustc convention.
Fatal when expansion is meaningless (returned through ExecEnv::finish_result); collected when usable output still exists (flushed by Logr::finish) so all problems of one item report in one pass.
Catalogue
Section titled “Catalogue”
Snapshot-tested diagnostics from packages/rsmack-ui-tests:
Macro Message after the prefix Trigger
edoc
Failed to read constants file `&lt;path&gt;`: No such file or directory (os error 2)
from points at a missing file
edoc
Unresolved const ident `NOPE`
Reference matches nothing
edoc
Only Tuple supported, maybe you are missing a second element
Payload is not a tuple
edoc
Unsupported const macro `vec!`
Element uses an unsupported macro
edoc
Ambiguous const `NAME`, qualify the path: `a::NAME`, `b::NAME`
Bare name matches several consts
megamac
Failed to get macro_impl_src of does_not_exist at `&lt;path&gt;`: No such file or directory (os error 2)
Missing impls/&lt;name&gt;.rs
megamac
Failed to parse macro_impl_src broken, this may happen for no real reason in your IDE, check that your project still builds with cargo: `<debug>``
Unparsable impl file
megamac
Unsupported MacroKind `Nope`, expected `Attr`, `Func` or `Derive`
Invalid kind
wrap
Only named struct supported
Tuple or unit struct
folder_iso_struct
Only named struct supported
Tuple or unit struct
seanum
Failed to generate TryFrom: variant `Plain` has fields, only unit variants are supported with integer `rs_type`
Non-unit variant with integer rs_type
Further collected (non-snapshotted) messages follow the same verbs — for example Cyclic const dependency involving `X` , Duplicate variant value `N`: discriminants must be unique for the generated `TryFrom` , and Failed to generate the migration helper: db_type `X` has no `ColumnDef` mapping.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
Handle macro errorsWrite diagnostics in this style for your own megamac macros.

# folder_iso_struct reference | rsmack

URL: /reference/folder-iso-struct/

folder_iso_struct reference
folder_iso_struct is an attribute macro — generated by megamac!(kind = Attr, name = folder_iso_struct, doc = "readme") — that mirrors a folder of Rust modules into a struct inline at expansion time. Crate path: rsmack_fs (facade: rsmack::folder_iso_struct, feature fs).
Signature
Section titled “Signature”
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[folder_iso_struct(folder </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"levels"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, vis </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"pub"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, recursive </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> true, derives(</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Debug"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">))]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Levels</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> { </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">...</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> }</span></div></div></code>
Arguments
Section titled “Arguments”
folder required
Section titled “folder required ”
Type: string literal
Meaning: folder to mirror, relative to the calling crate’s src/ — "levels" or "ui/screens"
Error: a missing folder is fatal — Failed to scan the folder to mirror '<path>': <reason>
vis optional
Section titled “vis optional ”
Type: string literal, e.g. "pub" or "pub(crate)"
Default: the annotated struct’s declared visibility
Meaning: visibility of every generated struct; invalid values are fatal — Invalid 'vis' value 'X', expected e.g. 'pub' or 'pub(crate)'
recursive optional
Section titled “recursive optional ”
Type: bool
Default: false
Meaning: subdirectories become inline pub mod <name> blocks holding their own mirrored struct, named after the PascalCase of the directory; in flat mode, directories become plain fields (legacy behavior)
derives optional
Section titled “derives optional ”
Type: list of string literals, parsed as paths
Default: empty
Meaning: extra derives injected on every generated struct, next to the annotated struct’s own attributes; invalid entries report Invalid 'derives' entry
Scanning rules
Section titled “Scanning rules”
The folder $CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/src/<folder> is scanned at expansion time — no build script, no OUT_DIR artifacts.
Entries sort deterministically; mod.rs is skipped.
Each file stem maps to a snake_case field name and a PascalCase type name: beta_gamma.rs → field beta_gamma, type BetaGamma. Keywords become raw idents.
Non-UTF-8 stems are reported.
Carry-over and references
Section titled “Carry-over and references”
The annotated struct’s attributes and visibility are copied onto every generated struct.
The declared fields are a sketch only and are discarded — the folder is the source of truth.
Mirror fields reference crate::<folder segments>::<mod>::<Type>, so the modules must exist in the calling crate’s module tree.
Tuple structs are fatal — Only named struct supported.
Example
Section titled “Example”
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">use</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">rsmack_fs</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">folder_iso_struct;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[folder_iso_struct(folder </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"levels"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, vis </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"pub"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, derives(</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Debug"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">))]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Levels</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// The declared fields are a sketch only: the mirror is generated from the folder.</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[expect(dead_code)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">alpha</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> (),</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
generates, for src/levels/{button.rs, beta_gamma.rs}:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[derive(</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Debug</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Levels</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> button</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">crate::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">levels</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">button</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Button</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> beta_gamma</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">crate::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">levels</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">beta_gamma</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">BetaGamma</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
Mirror a folderA task-focused guide with recursive mirroring.

# megamac reference | rsmack

URL: /reference/megamac/

megamac reference
megamac is a procedural macro that generates procedural macros. One megamac! call plus an impls/<name>.rs file yields a fully documented #[proc_macro], #[proc_macro_attribute], or #[proc_macro_derive] entrypoint. Crate path: rsmack_megamac (facade: rsmack::megamac, feature megamac). Authoring additionally requires a direct rsmack-utils dependency, because the generated code references rsmack_utils::exec::* drivers and ExecEnv.
Invocation
Section titled “Invocation”
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">megamac!</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(kind </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Attr</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, name </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> edoc, impls </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"impls"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, args </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Args"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, doc </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"readme"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">);</span></div></div></code>
Arguments
Section titled “Arguments”
kind required
Section titled “kind required ”
Type: Func | Attr | Derive
Meaning: function-like macro, attribute macro, or derive macro; anything else is fatal — Unsupported MacroKind 'X', expected 'Attr', 'Func' or 'Derive'
name required
Section titled “name required ”
Type: identifier
Meaning: the generated macro’s name; for kind = Derive, the derive is the PascalCase of name (type_name → #[derive(TypeName)])
impls optional
Section titled “impls optional ”
Type: identifier
Default: impls
Meaning: module directory that holds <name>.rs
args optional
Section titled “args optional ”
Type: identifier
Default: Args
Meaning: the darling payload struct in darling mode; setting it alongside a raw TokenStream signature is fatal
doc optional
Section titled “doc optional ”
Type: readme | inline | none
Default: inline
Meaning: readme embeds the calling crate’s README.md via include_str!; inline generates only the parameter docs; none emits no docs
The impl file convention
Section titled “The impl file convention”
The implementation lives at <src>/<impls>/<name>.rs (e.g. src/impls/greeting.rs) and contains a documented Args struct plus an exec function. Missing files are fatal — Failed to get macro_impl_src of <name> at <path>: <os error>; unparsable files report Failed to parse macro_impl_src <name>, this may happen for no real reason in your IDE, check that your project still builds with cargo.
Payload protocol — the signature is the configuration
Section titled “Payload protocol — the signature is the configuration”
The generated entrypoint reads the exec signature (the trailing &ExecEnv parameter is ignored):
exec signature Protocol Generated entrypoint
exec(args: Args, env: &ExecEnv) -> TokenStream
darling meta parsing, docs from Args
Func
exec(input: TokenStream, env: &ExecEnv) -> TokenStream
raw payload, DSL macros
Func
exec(args: Args, item: syn::Item, env: &ExecEnv) -> TokenStream
darling + parsed item
Attr
exec(input: TokenStream, item: syn::Item, env: &ExecEnv) -> TokenStream
raw payload + parsed item
Attr
exec(item: syn::DeriveInput, env: &ExecEnv) -> TokenStream
derive, no payload
Derive
The item type for Attr macros is inferred from the signature — no separate configuration. The args-struct ident follows the signature’s type name unless args = "..." overrides it.
Generated documentation
Section titled “Generated documentation”
For darling-mode Func and Attr macros:
The Args struct’s doc comment becomes the intro paragraph.
Each field doc becomes a # Parameters bullet: * `field` - `<doc>``` plus + type: [Ty]``.
Fields that are Option<T> or carry #[darling(default)] are marked (optional); undocumented fields read “Not documented”.
doc = "readme" prepends #[doc = include_str!("../README.md")].
The # Parameters section is omitted when there are no fields, in raw mode, for derives, and with doc = "none". A unit Args (pub struct Args;) is legitimate.
Configuration errors: a missing Args struct is fatal — Failed to find 'Args' struct in 'impls'; only named fields document — Unsupported 'Args' struct: only named fields are documented.
Memoization
Section titled “Memoization”
The impl-file analysis is cached per process keyed by (path, mtime, len, kind, args_override); cached fatals and issues replay identically on warm resolutions. Warm expansions measure 15–18 µs in the benchmarks.
Playground
Section titled “Playground”
Terminal window
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">cargo</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">run</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">-p</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">rsmack-megamac</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--bin</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">playground</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--kind</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">Attr</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--name</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">edoc</span></div></div></code>
Prints the expansion without compiling. Flags: --kind, --name (required), --src-dir (default $CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/src), --impls, --args, --doc.

# rsmack-utils reference | rsmack

URL: /reference/rsmack-utils/

rsmack-utils reference
rsmack-utils is the toolkit every macro in the workspace builds on: the ExecEnv/Logr diagnostics pair, five reusable entrypoint drivers, memoized filesystem helpers, and two exported macro_rules! helpers. It compiles without syn’s full feature; only crates that parse full items opt in.
ExecEnv
Section titled “ExecEnv”
The per-expansion environment handed to every exec function.
Member Signature Description
prefix
pub prefix: String
Diagnostic prefix, rendered #[<prefix>] <message>
logr
pub logr: Logr
The diagnostics collector owned by this expansion
new
new(prefix: impl Into<String>) -> Self
Plain constructor
finish
finish(&self, output: TokenStream) -> TokenStream
Appends all collected errors as compile_error! tokens and returns the output
finish_result
finish_result(&self, result: syn::Result<TokenStream>) -> TokenStream
Renders Ok as-is, or appends the error and flushes — the canonical idiom is env.finish_result(run(args, item, env))
Logr
Section titled “Logr”
The diagnostics collector. Lives for one proc-macro expansion; there is no panic path anywhere.
Method Signature Description
new
new(prefix: impl Into<String>) -> Self
Create a collector with a #[<prefix>] message prefix
error
error(&self, span: Span, msg: M) -> syn::Error (#[must_use])
Build a fatal error for ?-style returns
call_site_error
call_site_error(&self, msg: M) -> syn::Error
Fatal error spanning the whole invocation
emit_error
emit_error(&self, span: Span, msg: M)
Collect a non-fatal error; flush happens in finish
has_errors
has_errors(&self) -> bool
Whether any non-fatal error was collected
finish
finish(&self, output: TokenStream) -> TokenStream
Flush collected errors as compile_error! tokens appended to the output
Entrypoint drivers
Section titled “Entrypoint drivers”
Five generic drivers in rsmack_utils::exec; generated code routes through them.
Driver Shape
attr_entrypoint
(meta, item, prefix, exec) — darling meta, parsed item
attr_raw_entrypoint
(meta, item, prefix, exec) — darling meta, raw payload, parsed item
func_entrypoint
(meta, prefix, exec) — darling meta
func_raw_entrypoint
(input, prefix, exec) — raw payload
derive_entrypoint
(item, prefix, exec) — derive input, no payload
Empty attribute meta parses as an empty list, so bare #[my_macro] works with all-default args. Every parse failure becomes a prefixed compile_error!.
Filesystem helpers
Section titled “Filesystem helpers”
Helpers in rsmack_utils::fs, shared by the macros and available for your own build scripts.
Item Description
staleness_key(path) -> Option<(SystemTime, u64)>
The (mtime, len) cache key both memo caches validate against
calling_crate_dir() -> &'static Path
Memoized walk up from OUT_DIR to the nearest Cargo.toml; requires a build script to exist so OUT_DIR is set
package_src_folder() -> PathBuf
$CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/src
scan_modules(folder, recursive) -> Result<ModuleTree, String>
Deterministic folder scan that skips mod.rs
ModuleTree
{ fields: Vec<ModuleField>, dirs: Vec<(Ident, ModuleTree)> } with a render(...) method that emits the mirrored code
ModuleField
{ mod_ident, ty_ident } — snake_case field ident and PascalCase type ident
folder_iso_struct()
bon builder for the build-script flavor: .name(...), .pre(&TokenStream), .from_crate(...), .folder(...), .vis("pub"), .recursive(false), .log_enabled(false), .call() — writes <name>.rs into OUT_DIR
parse_id_maybe_raw(s) -> Ident
Parses keywords as raw idents
generate_file(path, bytes)
Writes a file into OUT_DIR
Exported macros
Section titled “Exported macros”
impl_json_schema!
Section titled “impl_json_schema!”
impl_json_schema!(UserId, "string") implements schemars::JsonSchema with a plain {"type": "string"} schema.
cl!
Section titled “cl!”
The code-link helper for doc comments: cl!(syn::Error) renders [`syn::Error`], cl!(syn::Error!) renders [`syn::Error!`], and cl!(Debug) renders Debug.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
Handle macro errorsFatal and collected diagnostics in practice.

# seanum reference | rsmack

URL: /reference/seanum/

seanum reference
seanum is an attribute macro — generated by megamac!(kind = Attr, name = seanum, doc = "readme") — that generates a SeaORM ActiveEnum from a plain Rust enum. Crate path: rsmack_seanum (facade: rsmack::seanum, feature seanum).
Signature
Section titled “Signature”
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[seanum(</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">rs_type </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"String"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">db_type </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"String(sea_orm::sea_query::StringLen::None)"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">rename_all </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"snake_case"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">derives(</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"::serde::Serialize"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"::serde::Deserialize"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">enum</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">SwitchAction</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> { </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">...</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> }</span></div></div></code>
Item arguments
Section titled “Item arguments”
rs_type required
Section titled “rs_type required ”
Type: syn::Ident
Meaning: the Rust type of the enum values ("String", "i32", …)
db_type required
Section titled “db_type required ”
Type: string literal
Meaning: the SeaORM column type, passed through to #[sea_orm(rs_type = ..., db_type = ...)]
derives optional
Section titled “derives optional ”
Type: list of string literals, parsed as paths
Default: empty
Meaning: extra derives appended after the defaults; invalid entries report Invalid 'derives' entry: {e}
migration optional
Section titled “migration optional ”
Type: bool
Default: false
Meaning: generates a migration_column_def() helper for sea-orm-migration
rename_all optional
Section titled “rename_all optional ”
Type: string literal — one of snake_case, camelCase, PascalCase, kebab-case, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, lowercase, UPPERCASE
Default: none — values keep their Rust names
Meaning: normalizes every non-renamed value; an unknown case is fatal
enum_name optional
Section titled “enum_name optional ”
Type: string literal
Default: the snake-cased enum name
Meaning: overrides the table name passed to #[sea_orm(enum_name = ...)]
Variant arguments
Section titled “Variant arguments”
rename optional
Section titled “rename optional ”
Type: string literal on a variant: #[seanum(rename = "send_email")]
Meaning: overrides rename_all for that variant; consumed from the output
Default derives
Section titled “Default derives”
Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, ::sea_orm::EnumIter, ::sea_orm::DeriveActiveEnum — minimal by design; serde/fake are opt-in through derives(...), never hidden dependencies.
Integer rs_type behavior
Section titled “Integer rs_type behavior”
When rs_type is one of i8–i64, u8–u64, isize, or usize:
The enum gains #[repr(rs_type)].
Every variant gains #[sea_orm(num_value = N)].
A value-based TryFrom<rs_type> is generated with type Error = ::sea_orm::DbErr.
Explicit discriminants are honored as integer literals (A = 10, B continues from 11; a leading - is accepted).
Duplicate values are collected as Duplicate variant value 'N': discriminants must be unique for the generated 'TryFrom' and the TryFrom is skipped.
Non-unit variants with an integer rs_type report Failed to generate TryFrom: variant 'X' has fields, only unit variants are supported with integer 'rs_type' and skip the TryFrom.
String rs_type values instead get #[sea_orm(string_value = "...")] per variant, with no TryFrom and no #[repr].
Migration helper
Section titled “Migration helper”
migration = true emits impl Enum { pub fn migration_column_def() -> ::sea_orm_migration::sea_query::ColumnDef }. The db_type maps to the ColumnDef method through this table:
String → string, Text → text, TinyInteger → tiny_integer, SmallInteger → small_integer, Integer → integer, BigInt → big_integer, TinyUnsigned → tiny_unsigned, SmallUnsigned → small_unsigned, Unsigned → unsigned, BigUnsigned → big_unsigned, Float → float, Double → double, Boolean → boolean, Date → date, DateTime → date_time, Json → json, JsonBinary → json_binary.
An unmapped db_type — including parameterized values such as "String(sea_orm::sea_query::StringLen::None)" — reports Failed to generate the migration helper: db_type 'X' has no 'ColumnDef' mapping.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
SeaORM enums (seanum)A task-focused guide with string and integer examples.
Edit page
Previous

# wrap reference | rsmack

URL: /reference/wrap/

wrap reference
wrap is an attribute macro — generated by megamac!(kind = Attr, name = wrap, doc = "readme") — that wraps every field of a named struct in a generic type. Crate path: rsmack_wrap (facade: rsmack::wrap, feature wrap).
Signature
Section titled “Signature”
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[wrap(with </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Option</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">User</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">name</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">String</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// Option<String></span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[wrap(skip)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">untouched</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">&</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">'</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">static</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">str</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
Item arguments
Section titled “Item arguments”
with required
Section titled “with required ”
Type: syn::Ident — accepted as a bare identifier or a string literal
Default: none, the argument is required
Meaning: the default wrapper applied to every field without per-field configuration
Example: with = Option or with = "Option"
Per-field arguments
Section titled “Per-field arguments”
Parsed from each #[wrap(...)] attribute on a field; the attribute is consumed from the output.
skip optional
Section titled “skip optional ”
Type: bool
Default: false
Meaning: leaves the field type untouched
with optional
Section titled “with optional ”
Type: syn::Ident
Default: inherits the item-level wrapper
Meaning: per-field wrapper override
Example: #[wrap(with = "Box")]
map optional
Section titled “map optional ”
Type: syn::Type
Default: none — the original inner type is kept
Meaning: replaces the inner type entirely
Example: #[wrap(with = "Vec", map = "u8")] turns String into Vec<u8>
Supported field types
Section titled “Supported field types”
The transformation parses Wrapper<Inner>, so every type expression wraps:
Field type With Option
String
Option<String>
Vec<T>
Option<Vec<T>>
&'static str
Option<&'static str>
*const u8
Option<*const u8>
fn(u8) -> bool
Option<fn(u8) -> bool>
Box<dyn Send>
Option<Box<dyn Send>>
(u8, u16)
Option<(u8, u16)>
[T; N]
Option<[T; N]>
Constraints and behavior
Section titled “Constraints and behavior”
Only named-field structs: tuple and unit structs are fatal — Only named struct supported.
Generics and where-clauses pass through untouched; only the fields are rewritten.
Non-wrap attributes are preserved. Place the macro before #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] so the derive observes the wrapped types.
Broken per-field attributes are collected as Failed to parse wrap attribute: {e} and stripped.
Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”
Wrap field typesA task-focused guide with serde ordering.

# Getting started | rsmack

URL: /tutorials/getting-started/

Getting started
In this tutorial you install rsmack, document a struct’s fields from constants with edoc, and wrap those fields in Option with wrap. You finish by reading the generated documentation in cargo doc.
Prerequisites
Section titled “Prerequisites”
Rust 1.94 or newer. Check with rustc --version and update with rustup update stable if needed.
Familiarity with basic Rust: structs, modules, and cargo commands.
1. Create a crate
Section titled “1. Create a crate”
Terminal window
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">cargo</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">new</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">rsmack-demo</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">cd</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">rsmack-demo</span></div></div></code>
2. Add the dependency
Section titled “2. Add the dependency”
One dependency brings every macro:
cargo add
Cargo.toml
Terminal window
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">cargo</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">add</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">rsmack</span></div></div></code>
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">[</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">dependencies</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">rsmack = </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"1"</span></div></div></code>
The rsmack facade re-exports all five macros behind its full feature (the default). To depend on a single macro instead, add rsmack with one feature — for example cargo add rsmack --no-default-features --features edoc — or depend on the standalone crate, such as rsmack-edoc.
3. Create a constants file
Section titled “3. Create a constants file”
edoc reads constants from a real file inside your crate’s src/ directory. Create src/consts.rs:
src/consts.rs
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">const</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">APP</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">&</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">str</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"myapp"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">const</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">MAJOR</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">i32</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">1</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">pub</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">const</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">TAG</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">&</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">str</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">concat!</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">(</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"v"</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">MAJOR</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">);</span></div></div></code>
4. Document a struct from the constants
Section titled “4. Document a struct from the constants”
Replace src/main.rs with:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">use</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">rsmack</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">edoc;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc(from </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> consts)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Client</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">/// Fallback docs: replaced by the edoc tuple below.</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[edoc((</span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"Client "</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">APP</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">" tag "</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">TAG</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">" build "</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, 2 </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">*</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> 21))]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">name</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">String</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">fn</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">main</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">() {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">let</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> _client </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Client</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> { name</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">"demo"</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">.</span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">to_string</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">() };</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
Each #[edoc((...))] tuple evaluates its elements — string literals, constant references, and const expressions such as 2 * 21 — and turns the concatenation into a real #[doc] attribute on the field. The element values keep their machine types (i128, f64, &str, …) until the docs are assembled.
Build once to make sure everything expands:
Terminal window
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">cargo</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">build</span></div></div></code>
The command returns without errors. If a constant is misspelled, the compiler reports #[rsmack_edoc::edoc] Unresolved const ident ... and every other broken expression on the item in the same pass.
5. Read the generated docs
Section titled “5. Read the generated docs”
Terminal window
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">cargo</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#032F62;--1:#9ECBFF">doc</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--no-deps</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#005CC5;--1:#79B8FF">--open</span></div></div></code>
Navigate to Client and then to the name field. The rendered text reads:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292e;--1:#e1e4e8">Client myapp tag v1 build 42</span></div></div></code>
APP renders as myapp, TAG resolves the const-to-const reference to v1, and the expression 2 * 21 evaluates to 42.
6. Wrap the fields
Section titled “6. Wrap the fields”
Add wrap to the same struct — or to a second struct, as here — and every field type is wrapped in the generic type you name:
<code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">use</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">rsmack</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">::</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">wrap;</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">#[wrap(with </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">Option</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">)]</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">struct</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">UserDraft</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">name</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">String</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// becomes Option<String></span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">email</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">String</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">, </span><span style="--0:#616972;--1:#99A0A6">// becomes Option<Vec<String>> for Vec fields, and so on</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code">
</div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">fn</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">main</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">() {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"> </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">let</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> draft </span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">=</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">UserDraft</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> {</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">name</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">None</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">email</span><span style="--0:#BF3441;--1:#F97583">:</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span><span style="--0:#6F42C1;--1:#B392F0">None</span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">,</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span class="indent"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8"> </span></span><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">};</span></div></div><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#24292E;--1:#E1E4E8">}</span></div></div></code>
The fields are now Option<String>. Per-field control is available with #[wrap(skip)], #[wrap(with = "Box")], and #[wrap(with = "Vec", map = "u8")] — see the wrap guide for the full behavior.
